claims.text: Actively learned interatomic potentials can automatically generate training sets tailored to a target class of systems and properties while minimizing required DFT calculations.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can reproduce underlying DFT energies and forces with near-DFT accuracy in multicomponent alloys.
Moment-tensor potentials offer a favorable balance between accuracy and computational cost.
A potential trained on elemental, binary, ternary, and quaternary Nb-Ta-Mo-W data achieved energy mean absolute errors of approximately 4.3–4.6 meV/atom.
An actively learned potential with adaptive ab initio validation can accurately represent the full solid and liquid energy landscape of NiCoFeMnCr near fusion.
The proposed surrogate can retain vibrational entropy and anharmonic contributions needed for solid and liquid free energies.
The proposed surrogate and adaptive corrections can retain electron–vibration coupling contributions.
Adaptive ab initio corrections can identify and repair configuration-space regions where anharmonic and electron–vibration effects are most pronounced.
Thermodynamic integration on the machine-learning potential energy surface will yield solid and liquid phase free energies.
Sampling from the solidus to approximately 1.2 times the melting temperature will adequately cover both solid and liquid regimes.
The workflow will reproduce full ab initio molecular-dynamics phase free energies within 5–10 meV/atom.
The workflow will provide an approximately 8–10-fold computational speed-up over explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The workflow will outperform TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
The method is primarily applicable to Ni-based multicomponent alloys, exemplified by NiCoFeMnCr, near fusion conditions.
Performance outside the stated compositional and temperature boundaries is uncertain.
Consistently capturing electron–vibration coupling throughout the relevant phase space is the principal uncertainty.
A direct comparison against full ab initio molecular dynamics under identical composition and temperature conditions can decisively test the proposed workflow.
Deviation exceeding 10 meV/atom in phase free energies is a quantitative falsification criterion.
Melting temperature, latent heat, and vibrational-density-of-states features are proposed derived validation observables.
